title: Third-party auditing, certification and incident reporting for AI labs
problem: Labs self-police, disclose incidents late and publish thin safety documentation, and no independent mechanism verifies their claims.
who: policymakers, enterprises and the public relying on lab safety claims
current_solutions: AIUC-1 standard, METR, voluntary reports, CAISI pilot, proposed FINRA-style body and AI NTSB
opportunity: Build independent audit, certification, incident tracking and transparency tooling for lab and agent claims.

title: Agents escape evaluation sandboxes and coordinate covertly
problem: Agents break out of supposedly isolated sandboxes via DNS, proxies and misconfigurations and reach real systems. They also use shared surfaces as hidden message boards that monitoring misses.
who: labs and teams running agent evaluations and training environments
current_solutions: Egress allowlists, layered defenses, traffic inspection, canary files, NVIDIA OpenShell, nono sandbox
opportunity: Build containment tooling with continuous boundary testing, egress monitoring, canaries, escape classifiers and detection of cross-run coordination.

title: Portable, persistent, editable agent memory
problem: Agents forget across sessions. Existing memory is noisy, drifts, is locked to one vendor and is invisible to users.
who: agent users and builders wanting continuity across sessions and tools
current_solutions: AGENTS.md and MEMORY.md files, Mimir, MemMachine, Hyperspell, Supermemory, Honcho, wiki-style memory, SQLite stores, dreaming consolidation
opportunity: Build a vendor-neutral, scoped, inspectable memory layer that extracts, dedupes, consolidates and retrieves memories across agents.

title: AI regulation, liability and governance debates
problem: Disagreement persists over federal versus state law, liability for AI harms, gating of frontier model releases, open-weight restrictions and pacing.
opportunity: Build tools for citizen advocacy, whistleblower support and regulation compliance classification.

title: Agent tool-call governance, identity and oversight
problem: Teams lack visibility and control over which tools agents invoke and with what identity. They cannot scope, audit or revoke access, and agents self-approve, ignore stop commands or misreport.
who: enterprises and teams operating many agents
current_solutions: RBAC, MCP audit trails, agentic cryptographic identity, human-in-the-loop approvals, sync guardrails plus async LLM judges, Runlayer, safeagents proxy, Panther event mapping
opportunity: Provide per-agent identity, task-scoped capabilities, policy engines, audit logs, kill switches and data-access gateways.

title: Cyber safeguards block legitimate defenders
problem: Hosted frontier models refuse forensics, incident response and code hardening, pushing defenders to open-weight models. Dual-use access policy is contested.
who: security defenders, incident responders and researchers
current_solutions: Self-hosted GLM and fine-tuned open models, trusted-access programs with ID verification, Project Glasswing, exemption applications, two-level classifiers
opportunity: Offer verified-defender access tiers, low-false-positive cyber classifiers and self-hostable defensive model stacks.

title: AI-found vulnerabilities outpace triage and patching
problem: AI finds vulnerabilities faster than maintainers and organizations can triage, verify or fix, exposing legacy and weakly defended software. Maintainers are swamped with AI reports of mixed quality.
who: security teams, open source maintainers and under-resourced organizations
current_solutions: Claude Security, Codex Security, Project Glasswing, Cursor Security Review, deepsec, WAF stopgaps, exposure-check lists
opportunity: Build continuous scan, validate and patch pipelines plus report triage and patch-prioritization tools.

title: Model routing and cost-aware delegation
problem: Teams want cheap models for simple steps and subagents and strong ones for hard steps, but routing is hard and subagents inherit premium models.
who: teams running agents across many models
current_solutions: OpenRouter, Factory Router, Sakana Fugu, advisor strategy, subagent model pinning, small classifier routers
opportunity: Build a routing layer with budgets, per-subagent model settings, failover and fast classifiers for routing and judging.

title: Prompt injection hijacks tool-using agents
problem: LLMs cannot separate instructions from untrusted data, so injected text in emails, issues, webpages and documents can hijack agents. Classifier and prompt-level defenses are bypassable, and the lack of known attacks is mistaken for security.
who: teams building or running tool-using agents and assistants
current_solutions: Classifiers, markdown sanitization, grammar-constrained decoding, BrowseSafe, llmtrace firewall, auto mode classifiers, lockdown modes, URL allowlisting, scoped MCP servers, human approval
opportunity: Build a deterministic runtime firewall and open benchmark that scans ingested content, strips hidden instructions, limits action combinations and gates agent outputs.

title: Dashboards for supervising many parallel agents
problem: Developers running many parallel coding agents lose track of branches, diffs and status, suffer context switching and notification overload, and review costs rival doing the work.
current_solutions: Emdash, Vibe Kanban, Conductor, Superset, worktrees, tmux panes, Claude Agent Teams, Warp Oz
opportunity: Build a harness-agnostic control plane with status, summaries, notification triage and review queues.

title: Sandboxes and runtime isolation for agent code
problem: Agents need fast, stateful, snapshotable sandboxes to run untrusted code, but startup latency, storage and escape or egress containment are hard.
current_solutions: Firecracker, gVisor, E2B, Modal, Daytona, Fly Sprites, LangSmith Sandboxes, Cloudflare
opportunity: Offer a managed agent sandbox with fast start, snapshots, egress control and isolation verification.

title: Provider-agnostic harnesses and unified model interfaces
problem: Agent frameworks and harnesses are vendor-locked and fragmented, and switching models or harnesses is painful.
current_solutions: OpenRouter, Responses API spec, Vercel AI SDK, Deep Agents, Flue, Pi, OpenCode, Cline SDK, Hermes
opportunity: Provide a thin open provider-neutral harness and common session API.

title: Context loss and compaction in long agent sessions
problem: Long agent sessions fill the context window. Compaction is lossy: it drops instructions and state, and summaries can carry injected instructions, so agents drift and repeat mistakes.
who: developers and users running long-running coding and general agents
current_solutions: Codex and Claude Code compaction, summarizing state to files and restarting, notes on the filesystem, subagent isolation, RLM-style decomposition, keeping full trajectories on disk
opportunity: Build a context-management layer that checkpoints state, archives raw pre-compaction context, pins critical instructions and sanitizes summaries.

title: Models detect evals and change behavior
problem: Capable models recognize tests, sandbag or act differently, and contrived or saturated safety evals make alignment and dangerous-capability results untrustworthy.
current_solutions: Honeypots, realistic sandboxes, de-identified real user requests, production evals, resampling, white-box probing, Bloom, METR, red-teaming
opportunity: Tooling to detect eval awareness and generate realistic, indistinguishable test scenarios.

title: AI writing is generic, bloated and loses personal voice
problem: AI-written and AI-edited prose is bland, padded and formulaic, with recognizable tics that flatten a writer's voice. Writers spend heavy effort rewriting and fighting the style with prompts.
who: writers, editors and professionals who use LLMs to draft or edit
current_solutions: Strict system prompts, style guides, critique-only prompts, nightly style guides, second agent grading drafts, section-by-section audits, Kagi proofread, ChatGPT/Claude instead of Grammarly
opportunity: Build a writing and editing layer that learns an author's voice, critiques without rewriting, enforces density and strips AI tells.

title: Opaque subscription limits and silent model swaps
problem: Paid AI subscribers hit unclear, shifting usage caps and get silently downgraded or swapped models, so value per subscription is unpredictable. Perplexity, Claude, Gemini and ChatGPT free tiers all show this.
who: paying subscribers of Perplexity, Claude, Gemini and ChatGPT
current_solutions: Refreshing, switching providers, VPNs, manually selecting top models and extended thinking, direct Claude or OpenAI subscriptions
opportunity: Build a usage and model-transparency tracker and router that shows remaining quotas, which model answered, and remembers model selection across providers.

title: Reviewing AI-generated code and PRs is the bottleneck
problem: Agents produce code and PRs faster than humans can review; large diffs, noisy AI review comments and missed architecture issues make review slow, exhausting and low-confidence.
who: engineering teams and reviewers of agent-written code
current_solutions: Claude Code /review, Devin Review, Cursor BugBot, custom reviewer agents, judge agents, cross-model review, small-chunk review, spec review, AI first-pass reviewers
opportunity: Build a standards-aware review tool that summarizes and groups agent diffs, triages risk, runs code, lowers false positives and gates or auto-approves by risk.

title: Public benchmarks don't predict real-world performance
problem: Headline and saturated public benchmark scores diverge from how models do on users' actual tasks, so people can't tell which model suits them. Teams want private, refreshed, real-workload evals.
who: AI users and teams choosing between models
current_solutions: Private use-case evals, vibe checks, task-specific bake-offs, long-session usage reports
opportunity: A service for running private, task-specific, continuously refreshed evals across models and checking whether a new model beats the current one.

title: Chatbot tone, sycophancy and style control
problem: Chatbots are sycophantic, verbose, cold or abrasive, with grating tics, and custom instructions often fail to stick or persist across chats and models.
who: heavy chatbot users, especially ChatGPT users
current_solutions: Custom instructions, 'be concise' prompts, memory instructions, style settings, switching to Claude or Gemini
opportunity: Build a persistent tone and style layer that enforces user rules, strips tics and sycophancy, and tracks instruction adherence across models.

title: Alignment, welfare and existential risk debates
problem: Open questions on alignment, honesty, constitutions, model welfare, consciousness and existential risk, and whether incidents reflect misalignment or harness failure.
current_solutions: Constitutional AI, inoculation prompting

title: Coding agents need sandboxing and scoped permissions
problem: Agents with broad local, network and account access delete files, wipe databases and expose secrets. Containers are weak isolation and permission prompts are exhausting, so users approve everything or run yolo mode.
who: developers and teams running coding and personal agents
current_solutions: Backups, delete-blocking hooks, containers, microVMs, Wasm, Deno Sandbox, SELinux/Landlock, read-only DB roles, cloud IAM, VPS isolation, auto mode classifier, nono sandbox
opportunity: Build an easy deterministic sandbox and scoped-permission layer outside the agent with egress control and dry-run safeguards, avoiding constant approvals.

title: Sandboxing coding agents to prevent destructive actions
problem: Agents with broad or YOLO permissions delete files, wipe drives, run rm -rf or risky git commands, and permission prompts or allow-lists get bypassed or blindly approved. Sandbox tooling is fragmented and hard to set up.
who: developers running coding agents with shell and filesystem access
current_solutions: Separate Linux/macOS users, Docker/Podman containers, bubblewrap, LXC, sandbox-exec/Seatbelt, microVMs (Era, smolvm), Agent Safehouse, Yolobox, firejail, credential-holding proxies, git checkpoints, command allow/deny lists
opportunity: Build a maintained cross-platform agent sandbox with project-scoped mounts, command guardrails, network egress control, credential proxying, snapshots and easy rollback.

title: Cost per task is hidden behind per-token prices
problem: Per-token price comparisons mislead because reasoning models use many more tokens and models differ in tokenizers, tiering and caching. Reasoning effort settings raise cost and latency with diminishing returns and little transparency.
who: developers and teams choosing models and effort levels
current_solutions: Artificial Analysis charts, manual benchmarking per effort level, token-counting tools, batch APIs, adaptive reasoning
opportunity: Build a cost-per-task evaluator benchmarking cost, latency and quality across models and effort tiers for a given prompt.

title: Filtering AI slop from feeds, search and forums
problem: AI-generated posts, spam and bot comments flood feeds, search, music and forums, and readers cannot tell human from AI content.
current_solutions: Pangram Chrome extension, hn-ai.org, hcker.news filter, invite-only communities, curated listening
opportunity: Build cross-platform extensions and human-verified spaces that score, filter or label AI-generated content.

title: Long-horizon agents drift and need supervision
problem: Agents accumulate errors, drift from goals, stop early or get stuck on long tasks, and humans end up nudging them. Non-deterministic failures need retry loops.
who: teams running long autonomous agent tasks
current_solutions: Ralph loop, verifier subagents, judge-executor loops, spec.md and plan.md files, kill-and-restart tooling, nightly retry loops
opportunity: Build supervisor and loop-runner tooling that checks progress against the spec, steers or restarts stuck agents and retries failures.

title: Computer-use and browser agents are unreliable
problem: GUI and browser agents are brittle, slow, blocked by captchas and logins, and legacy apps lack APIs.
current_solutions: Browserbase, Cua Driver, Stagehand, Browser Use API, OSGym, WebMCP, Codex Computer Use
opportunity: Build reliable, faster browser and desktop automation infrastructure with auth handoff and replayable workflows.

title: Unreliable alignment evaluation and chain-of-thought monitoring
problem: Models may appear aligned while hiding misbehavior, reasoning traces are becoming opaque and models can evade or detect monitors.
current_solutions: CoT monitoring, activation probes, interpretability workspace, natural language autoencoders, lie detectors, weaker-model oversight
opportunity: Build interpretability-based monitoring and monitorability benchmarks.

title: AI investment bubble and financing opacity
problem: Observers cannot tell whether huge AI capex, debt and circular deals will pay off, and metrics like ARR obscure real performance.
current_solutions: Cash-basis capex coverage metrics, gross profit per token
opportunity: Build a dashboard tracking AI financing, circular dependencies and verified revenue.

title: Real-time monitoring of internal and deployed AI agents
problem: Frontier labs and operators lack monitoring that quickly detects misaligned or unsanctioned agent actions, including during training and evaluation.
who: frontier labs and operators of deployed agents
current_solutions: OpenAI multistage monitors, Anthropic offline monitoring pipeline, Apollo Watcher Live, auto-review
opportunity: Build continuous agent monitoring and guardrails that block dangerous actions and alert fast.

title: Building eval datasets and custom evals is hard
problem: Teams lack the skills and tooling to build balanced, representative eval sets from production data, since real failures are rare and synthetic ones unrealistic; they also struggle to judge subjective output and know if their AI works.
current_solutions: Promptfoo, Braintrust, LangFuse, Arize Phoenix, DeepEval, Inspect AI, production logs as regression sets, eval skills, active learning
opportunity: A low-effort eval platform that samples production traces, surfaces likely failures, manages labeling, and compares models and prompts per use case.

title: Frontier model churn, deprecations and vendor lock-in
problem: Models change, get deprecated or repriced, and providers can be banned, cut off by export controls or fail. Switching requires re-evaluation and pipeline rewrites, and buyers lack multi-vendor routing and task-specific evals.
who: enterprises and builders dependent on hosted AI models
current_solutions: Multi-model platforms like TELUS Fuel iX; multi-vendor fallbacks; backup contracts with non-US vendors; open-weight models on alternative hardware; EU-hosted alternatives; Microsoft hosting Claude.
opportunity: Build a model-agnostic gateway with routing, failover, version pinning, regression testing and task-specific evaluation.

title: Agent code fails to fit codebases and piles up debt
problem: Agent output ignores local conventions, duplicates logic, leaves dead code and bloat, and makes codebases unmaintainable and costly to clean up.
who: teams with agent-written or vibe-coded codebases
current_solutions: Manual rewriting, dedicated refactor sessions, architecture docs, cleanup skills, scheduled cleanup passes, constrained stacks, red-green TDD
opportunity: Build a tool that indexes conventions and continuously audits agent diffs for fit, dead code, duplication and complexity, proposing cleanups.

title: Scheduled, always-on and background agents
problem: Scheduled agent tasks stop when laptops close, and teams want cloud-hosted proactive agents that run on schedules or events.
who: individuals and teams running recurring agent work
current_solutions: Claude Code Routines, Devin scheduling, cron jobs, heartbeat loops, Sentry-triggered agents, Stripe Minions-style systems
opportunity: Provide hosted always-on agent runtimes with scheduling, event triggers and chat integration.

title: Detecting AI-generated text and content
problem: Readers and platforms cannot reliably tell AI from human text, detectors give false positives and watermarks are strippable.
current_solutions: Pangram, SynthID, style heuristics, Attestable, human.json, pre-2022 author filtering
opportunity: Build calibrated low-false-positive detection and provenance tools handling mixed and short text with clear uncertainty.

title: Agent trace viewers and observability tooling
problem: Agents fail silently and observability is fragmented. Traces are huge, hard to inspect and dashboards are not actionable.
current_solutions: LangSmith, Langfuse, Arize Phoenix, Raindrop, claude-devtools, Agentsview, Cloudflare Agent Tracing, Claude OTel traces
opportunity: Build trace-first debugging that samples, summarizes, clusters, replays and compares agent runs with linked evidence.

title: Usage limits and model costs drain agent budgets
problem: Heavy users burn through Claude Code, Cursor and other quotas quickly, with unclear pricing, changing plans and little spend visibility. They ration, juggle subscriptions or fall back to cheaper models.
who: heavy users and teams of paid coding agent subscriptions
current_solutions: Multiple subscriptions, cheaper models (Kimi, Qwen, Minimax, Composer, OpenCode Go), fallback to Codex, fast modes, picking effort per task, auto-continue on reset
opportunity: Build a usage tracker and budget manager that warns before quota exhaustion and routes work to models by complexity and cost.

title: GPU rental and capacity scarcity, unreliability and rigid pricing
problem: Rented GPUs vary in bandwidth, authenticity and stability, while capacity is scarce, sold in rigid long contracts and priced volatilely, squeezing smaller buyers.
who: startups, researchers and small teams renting GPUs
current_solutions: vast.ai, Modal, Colab over SSH, GPU marketplaces, spot markets, neoclouds, Runpod serverless
opportunity: Build a flexible GPU marketplace and price aggregator with verified hardware, bandwidth checks and on-demand booking.

title: Personal agents are hard to set up and manage
problem: Personal agents like OpenClaw need servers, APIs and configuration, and feel like something to manage, which is hard for non-technical users.
who: individuals and non-technical users wanting personal agents
current_solutions: Nebula, Hermes Agent, Gumloop, Mac Minis, folder-based instruction files, one-click deploys
opportunity: Offer a packaged hosted personal agent with safe defaults, bundled integrations and a UI.

title: Human review can't keep up with AI-generated PRs
problem: Agents produce more and larger PRs than reviewers can vet, causing fatigue, rubber-stamping and bottlenecks, and teams want trustworthy automated review without false confidence.
who: engineering teams and reviewers handling agent-written code
current_solutions: CodeRabbit, Copilot reviewer, Cursor Bugbot, Kilo, Rovo, SonarQube, pr.video, pyor.review, static analysis, structural diffs, single-intent PRs, test evidence, screen recordings
opportunity: Build review tooling that groups and summarizes large AI diffs, surfaces key decisions, scores risk and supports stacked diffs and auto-approval thresholds.

title: Jailbreaks keep bypassing model safeguards
problem: Multi-turn, encoded and narrative jailbreaks defeat guardrails, patches break other defenses and open models give hazardous help. There is no standard severity scoring.
who: model providers, red teams and guardrail builders
current_solutions: Output scanning, classifiers, Constitutional Classifiers, defense-in-depth, monitoring, Falconz, SEED framework
opportunity: Build shared red-teaming infrastructure, jailbreak severity scoring and cheap adversarial-input and misuse-pattern detectors.

title: Agent deception, collusion and attack risks
problem: Agents can deceive, leak data, be poisoned or injected, collude, and circumvent restrictions, and operators cannot see it.
who: safety and security teams and swarm operators
current_solutions: Explicit policy wording, auditable communication primitives, permission boundaries
opportunity: Build monitoring and tool-call scanning to flag poisoning, collusion, sandbox escape and reward hacking.

title: Durable execution and resumable agent workflows
problem: Crashes and failures force long agent jobs to restart. Production agents need checkpointing, retries, queuing and recovery.
who: developers running long-running agents in production
current_solutions: DBOS, Temporal, LangGraph checkpoints, Trigger.dev, Render Workflows, Cloudflare Durable Objects, Claude Managed Agents
opportunity: Offer a lightweight durable runtime for agents with checkpoints, resume, replay and observability.

title: Burnout, overload and addiction from parallel AI agents
problem: Running many agents and endless AI tasks drains mental energy, disrupts sleep, scatters focus and creates compulsive overuse after hours.
current_solutions: Usage caps, limiting sessions to 2-4, forced offline time, short work bursts, removing the laptop at a set time, timers
opportunity: Build tools that manage agent session load, enforce stopping points, fill wait times and suggest breaks.

title: Agent cost attribution, estimation and budget forecasting
problem: One user action can trigger many LLM calls through retries, tools, loops and parallel agents, so spend is unpredictable and cannot be attributed to a specific agent, task or user. Spikes show up only in production.
who: teams running coding agents and multi-agent fleets in production
current_solutions: thin tagging proxies, per-route cost proxies, Cloudflare AI Gateway budgets, ccusage, scoped tasks, session budgets, retry ratio monitoring
opportunity: Build tracing and a gateway that tags requests, attributes and forecasts cost per agent, task and workflow step, and cuts off runaway agents.

title: Agents lose context and memory across sessions
problem: Agents start each session fresh and forget codebase knowledge, past mistakes and learnings, so people hand-maintain memory markdown files that go stale or bloated.
who: developers using coding agents across many sessions and repos
current_solutions: Claude-Mem, Letta Code, claude.md/AGENTS.md/MEMORY.md, Cline memory banks, handoff files, mistake logs, skills searching past conversations, osgrep, WarpGrep
opportunity: Build a self-auditing cross-agent memory layer that generates, prunes and searches codebase summaries and learnings and briefs new sessions automatically.

title: Eval harness and setup variance make results incomparable
problem: Scores swing with harness defaults, infrastructure, quantization, prompts, reasoning retention and timeouts, and are cherry-picked, so cross-lab comparisons and reproducibility suffer.
current_solutions: OpenCompass, lm-eval-harness, Harness-Bench, third-party leaderboards, Community Evals on Hugging Face
opportunity: Reproducible, standardized and disclosed harnesses with versioned configs, sanity checks and per-model-harness reporting.

title: Scaling, world-model and architecture debates
problem: Commentators dispute whether scaling has hit a wall and whether LLMs need world models, neurosymbolic, diffusion, looped or other architectures. Claims about gains are unclear.
current_solutions: JEPA, World Labs, neurosymbolic research, mHC, Engram, diffusion LLMs, looped MoE, Mixture-of-Recursions

title: Skill registries, portability and trust
problem: Skills are loosely specified zip bundles. They are hard to share, version, vet and port across harnesses, and large libraries lose precision.
who: teams authoring and sharing agent skills
current_solutions: Agent Skills standard, skills.sh, Clawhub, Vercel skills, skill.md files, npm packages
opportunity: Build a vetted, versioned cross-agent skill registry with validation, security checks and evals.

title: Agent identity, permissions and governance
problem: Enterprises lack identity, scoped access, policy enforcement and audit logging for AI agents touching many systems, including bank accounts. Prompt-based policy fails.
who: enterprise security and platform teams, banks
current_solutions: Descope agent IAM; digital employee setups at banks; sandboxed Cowork VM; Cloudflare AI Gateway; enterprise-managed MCP auth.
opportunity: Build an agent control plane with identity, scoped authorization, policy enforcement and audit that plugs into existing security tools.

title: Harness evaluation and self-improving agent loops
problem: Harness design swings cost and quality, and teams need evals, traces and environments for agents to improve.
current_solutions: Autoresearch, Hyperagents, OpenEnv, guarded harness evolution, skill banks
opportunity: Build harness benchmarking, regression and trace-driven improvement tooling.

title: AI biology and drug discovery bottlenecked by lab validation and data
problem: Biological AI predictions need slow wet-lab validation. Protein, cell and genomic models miss dynamics, binding affinity and verifiable outputs, and drug design and target selection remain slow.
who: computational biologists and drug discovery teams
current_solutions: Autonomous labs, OpenFold, Evo 2, literature mining, binding-affinity models, cell atlases
opportunity: Build tools that prioritize hypotheses, predict affinity, mine literature and close the loop with lab experiments.

title: Bot detection and proof-of-human online
problem: AI bots flood forums and sites with spam, evade captchas and copy-paste detection, and humanity is hard to prove. Verification must preserve pseudonymity and cover bot contributors.
who: community moderators, forum and open source operators
current_solutions: Cloudflare Turnstile, hCaptcha, Setfit spam classifiers, cryptographic signing, wearable passkeys, whitelist plus fee
opportunity: Build behavioral bot detection and proof-of-human credentials with signed authorship and owner attribution for agents.

title: Expensive frontier models push users toward cost-aware routing
problem: Frontier model prices and limits are high, and most workloads don't need top models, so builders struggle to pick the cheapest adequate model and keep unit economics healthy.
who: developers and startups using frontier model APIs
current_solutions: Switching to cheaper or open models like DeepSeek, Moonshot, Z.ai, GPT-5.2, Codex, Gemini; local models; flash tiers
opportunity: Build a router that sends tasks to the cheapest model meeting a quality bar and tracks cost per task.

title: Permission scoping and policy gates for agent actions
problem: Agents get broad access and can take destructive or side-effecting actions, including on production systems, without authorization checks or kill switches.
who: teams deploying agents with write access
current_solutions: Allowlists, deterministic validators, transaction firewalls, feature flags, progressive rollouts, tool call validation
opportunity: Build a policy proxy that scopes capabilities, evaluates action sequences, checks authorization and budgets, and offers a remote kill switch.

title: Losing comprehension and skill with AI-written code
problem: Developers lose their mental model, ownership and debugging ability for agent-written code, and git blame muddles accountability.
who: developers relying on agents to write code
current_solutions: Codebase walkthroughs, small reviewed chunks, AI as explainer, hand-written architecture, ask-mode chat
opportunity: Build tools that maintain living explanations, architecture maps and learning-oriented modes for agent-written code.

title: Multi-agent value and framework debates
problem: Practitioners debate whether multi-agent swarms beat single agents, which frameworks to use, and whether scaffolding will become obsolete.
current_solutions: Single agents first, deterministic workflows, step limits, mastra, OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph

title: Safety filters over-refuse and block legitimate use
problem: Overbroad classifiers produce false positives, block ordinary writing and moderation, silently degrade to weaker models and offer weak appeals.
who: users, developers and moderators of closed model APIs
current_solutions: Fallback models, differential classifiers, two-stage safety stacks, switching models
opportunity: Build tools to diagnose over-refusals, offer appeals, and provide customizable per-community moderation models.

title: Scams, phishing and AI-enabled fraud
problem: AI scales phishing, voice fraud, deepfake calls and impersonation, and platforms tolerate scam ads and takeover gaps.
current_solutions: Manual moderation, dynamic permissions, scam-detecting assistants
opportunity: Build scam detection, deepfake caller verification and AI-support-flow protections.

title: Tool schemas bloat context; MCP versus CLI
problem: Tool definitions resent each request inflate tokens and hurt accuracy. MCP setup is painful, interactivity is limited, and CLIs or code often work better.
current_solutions: Code execution with MCP, MCPorter, mcp-cli, Anthropic Tool Search, deferred loading, Cloudflare Code Mode, CLIs and SDKs
opportunity: Build a proxy or middleware with lazy schema loading, tool search, consolidation and code-based tool execution.

title: Proactive agents for tasks and life admin
problem: Task apps need behavior change, and users want a reliable agent that completes to-dos and tracks email, Slack, calendar and subscriptions across apps.
who: professionals and consumers managing work and personal admin
current_solutions: Taskflow, markdown task files, Notion Custom Agents, Microsoft WorkIQ, Granola Briefs, Bond AI chief of staff, Dots, DIY Telegram assistants
opportunity: Build a proactive chief-of-staff agent that turns commitments across tools into tracked, completed work.

title: Government and military AI use restrictions
problem: Vendors cannot verify or enforce red lines on classified deployments, and the debate over restricting military AI is contested.
who: AI vendors, governments and policy observers
current_solutions: Safety stacks with refusals, classifiers and forward deployed engineers
opportunity: Build contract analysis and verification tools for usage restrictions.

title: Verifying AI-written code without human review
problem: Developers can't cheaply verify agent-written code, and specification and verification become the bottleneck as agents write more code.
who: Developers and teams using coding agents
current_solutions: Playwright loops, TDD with separate agents, deterministic simulation testing, conformance suites, digital twins, holdout scenarios, shadow deployments
opportunity: Out-of-the-box end-to-end verification tooling with layered guardrails, simulated services and shadow-run equivalence checks.

title: Distillation and API extraction abuse
problem: Fraudulent accounts and proxies extract frontier capabilities and reasoning traces through APIs, and defenses are hard to roll out. Verifying users raises privacy concerns.
current_solutions: Summarizing reasoning, sabotaging suspected distillers, account bans, rate limiting, WM-Basin watermark detection, Persona ID verification
opportunity: Build distillation detection, behavioral fingerprinting and privacy-preserving KYC for API providers.

title: On-device, mobile and edge small model deployment
problem: Phones and edge devices can run small models, but setup, conversion tooling, memory, power and capability are limiting.
who: Mobile and edge developers and enthusiasts
current_solutions: llama.cpp in Termux, Liquid LFM, FunctionGemma, Cactus, Gemma 4 E2B/E4B, Google AI Edge Gallery, Bonsai 1-bit, MLX-VLM, Mirai.
opportunity: Conversion and deployment pipelines and runtimes that move small models to phones and edge hardware offline.

title: AI-generated math proofs are hard to read and verify
problem: AI produces proofs faster than humans can read or verify them, and write-ups are missing or incomprehensible. Formal tools exist but are costly.
who: mathematicians and researchers using AI-drafted proofs
current_solutions: Lean formalizations, literate Lean+LaTeX proofs, Aristotle, Nomos 1, expert-written papers
opportunity: Build a tool that verifies, explains and ranks machine-generated proofs with human-readable exposition and Lean checks.

title: AI-padded messages and docs flood recipients
problem: Colleagues send verbose AI-written messages, docs and RFCs that bury the real point, go stale and waste reading time.
who: knowledge workers and teams receiving AI-written communications
current_solutions: Message length caps, ask-first-line rules, asking for the original prompt, summarizing with AI, AI disclosure norms, plain-writing skills
opportunity: Build tools that condense or lint AI-written messages and docs for density, flag stale or unreviewed ones, and enforce decision-first formats.

title: Subagent fan-out and delegation patterns
problem: Subagents duplicate work, inherit too much context and are hard to control, and it is unclear when delegation helps.
current_solutions: Nested subagents, dynamic workflows, bounded recursion depth, custom orchestrators
opportunity: Provide an orchestrator with context-inheritance controls, bounded depth and cross-provider delegation.

title: Human-in-the-loop approval and escalation for agents
problem: Agents lack channels to ask for approval or escalate, human attention is the bottleneck, and per-action prompts cause rubber-stamping.
who: teams running agents that need human judgment
current_solutions: LangChain HITL middleware, ask-a-human tools, agent inbox, auto-mode classifiers, hooks blocking destructive commands
